newsitem.title: CHINA: Cambodia king calls for immediate end to fighting.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia king calls for immediate end to fighting.

text.p: Cambodian King Sihanouk on Sunday called for an immediate end to fighting in Phnom Penh, saying the country's rival prime ministers should quickly visit him in Beijing to iron out their differences.
"Please stop fighting right away without any preconditions," Sihanouk said in a unofficial translation of a statement to the rival FUNCINPEC and Cambodian People's Party.

Forces loyal to Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh and his former battlefield enemy, Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, fought for a second day in the Cambodian capital on Sunday, and Sihanouk said the situation was grave.
The king called on both prime ministers and president of parliament Chea Sim to come to Beijing, where Sihanouk has a residence and has been receiving medical treatment.

"I request His Excellency Chea Sim, His Highness Prince Ranariddh and His Excellency Hun Sen to please come to see me right away at my residence in Beijing so that we can together solve these most serious problems," he said.
The two prime ministers head a fractured coalition government formed after a United Nations-run election in 1993.
